description: Open flat palm raised to temple and waved gently outwards.
instructions:
1. Raise dominant open hand to temple height.
2. Extend fingers with palm facing outwards.
3. Wave hand gently away from the forehead.
exampleUsage: Used as a friendly initial greeting when meeting someone.

description: Flat hand fingertips touch chin/lips then move forward towards person.
instructions:
1. Place fingers of flat dominant hand on your chin or lips.
2. Move the hand outward and slightly down toward the other person.
3. Maintain a warm facial expression.
exampleUsage: Used to express gratitude, appreciation, or politeness.

description: Sign 'Good' from chin to flat palm, then rise hand like rising sun.
instructions:
1. Touch chin with flat hand and bring down to non-dominant palm ('Good').
2. Place non-dominant arm horizontal, and bring dominant hand up under it like the rising sun ('Morning').
exampleUsage: Standard polite morning greeting.

description: Sign 'Good', then bring flat hand downward slightly past horizontal arm.
instructions:
1. Sign 'Good' from chin to palm.
2. Place dominant forearm resting at 45 degrees over horizontal base arm indicating midday sun position.
exampleUsage: Greeting used during noon and afternoon hours.

description: Sign 'Good', then curve dominant wrist over non-dominant horizontal arm.
instructions:
1. Sign 'Good' from chin to palm.
2. Rest dominant curved hand over the edge of the horizontal base arm representing the sun setting.
exampleUsage: Used when parting in the evening or going to sleep.

description: Both hands knuckles together roll outward to thumbs up, then point forward.
instructions:
1. Place both curved hands knuckles touching against chest.
2. Roll hands outward so palms face upward ('How').
3. Point index finger directly at the conversational partner ('You').
exampleUsage: Inquiring about someone's state of well-being.

description: Open hand with thumb touching chest repeatedly.
instructions:
1. Open dominant hand with spread fingers ('5' handshape).
2. Tap thumb lightly against center of chest twice.
exampleUsage: Responding positively to 'How are you?'.

description: Raise index finger pointing upward while making slight circular pause gesture.
instructions:
1. Raise dominant index finger pointing up (indicating 'One').
2. Keep palm facing inward slightly and hold position momentarily.
exampleUsage: Asking someone to wait a brief second.

description: Make a fist and nod it up and down like a head nodding.
instructions:
1. Form an 'S' fist with dominant hand.
2. Tilt wrist forward and back in a nodding motion twice.
exampleUsage: Affirmative agreement or consent.

description: Snap index and middle fingers down onto the thumb.
instructions:
1. Extend index and middle finger together with thumb outstretched.
2. Snap the two fingers firmly against the thumb pad.
exampleUsage: Denial, refusal, or negative response.

description: Flat palm on center of chest rubbed in clockwise circular motion.
instructions:
1. Place flat open dominant hand over chest center.
2. Rub hand in circular motion clockwise two or three times.
exampleUsage: Polite request for assistance or favors.

description: Fist rubbed in circular motion over center of chest.
instructions:
1. Form an 'A' fist with dominant hand.
2. Rub fist in a circular motion on center of chest with an apologetic expression.
exampleUsage: Apologizing for an accident, mistake, or inconvenience.

description: Thumbs-up fist placed on flat non-dominant palm, raised upwards together.
instructions:
1. Make a 'thumbs-up' fist with dominant hand.
2. Place it on top of flat non-dominant palm facing up.
3. Lift both hands upward together.
exampleUsage: Requesting immediate assistance or aid.

description: Sign 'I', then bent index finger pulled towards chest ('Need'), then sign 'Help'.
instructions:
1. Point index finger to chest ('I').
2. Bend index finger ('X' handshape) and pull downward ('Need').
3. Lift thumbs-up fist on flat palm toward chest ('Help me').
exampleUsage: Urgent emergency communication when requiring medical or general help.

description: Flat hand touches chin and drops onto flat non-dominant palm.
instructions:
1. Place fingers of flat dominant hand on lips/chin.
2. Bring hand down firmly into palm of flat non-dominant hand.
exampleUsage: Expressing approval, positive quality, or satisfaction.

description: Flat hand touches chin and flips outward/downward turning palm down.
instructions:
1. Place fingers of flat dominant hand on chin.
2. Move hand away and flip wrist so palm faces down towards the floor.
exampleUsage: Expressing displeasure, poor quality, or disapproval.

description: Form 'W' handshape (3 fingers up) and tap index finger against chin.
instructions:
1. Make a 'W' handshape with index, middle, and ring fingers extended.
2. Tap the side of index finger twice against the chin.
exampleUsage: Requesting drinking water.

description: Flattened 'O' handshape tapped twice against lips.
instructions:
1. Touch all fingertips to thumb pad forming a beak shape ('flattened O').
2. Tap fingertips against lips twice.
exampleUsage: Communicating hunger or asking for food/meal.

description: Chop edge of flat dominant hand down firmly into non-dominant palm.
instructions:
1. Hold non-dominant hand flat, palm facing up.
2. Bring edge of flat dominant hand down sharply like a chop onto the open palm.
exampleUsage: Halting an action, warning of immediate danger, or ending speech.

description: Thumbs-up hands with dominant thumb flicking up repeatedly past other fist.
instructions:
1. Make two 'A' fists with thumbs pointing upward.
2. Brush the back of dominant thumb upwards across non-dominant fist repeatedly.
exampleUsage: Warning someone of hazardous conditions or threats.

description: Hand with thumb, index finger, and pinky finger extended simultaneously.
instructions:
1. Extend thumb, index finger, and pinky finger from fist (combination of I, L, and Y).
2. Hold hand facing outward at chest height.
exampleUsage: Expressing affection, love, and care.

description: Open hand with palm facing up swept in arc toward body.
instructions:
1. Hold dominant hand out to the side with open palm facing up.
2. Sweep hand in an arc towards the center of your chest.
exampleUsage: Welcoming guests or responding to 'Thank You'.

description: Slide dominant palm across non-dominant palm, then bring two index fingers together.
instructions:
1. Slide flat dominant palm across flat base palm ('Nice').
2. Bring two pointing index fingers together facing each other ('Meet').
3. Point to partner ('You').
exampleUsage: Introductions when meeting someone for the first time.

description: 'T' handshape (thumb between index and middle) shaken side to side.
instructions:
1. Form a 'T' handshape by tucking thumb under index finger knuckle.
2. Shake hand gently from side to side.
exampleUsage: Asking for bathroom/washroom location.

description: Tap curved 'M' or 'D' fingertips against inner wrist where pulse is felt.
instructions:
1. Hold non-dominant wrist with palm facing up.
2. Tap bent fingertips of dominant hand twice against the inner pulse point of wrist.
exampleUsage: Requesting medical attention or visiting a physician.
